```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

**Status.** Figure 1 is *descriptive*. Each plotted point is a model-estimated inoculated-minus-sterile
contrast with an unadjusted 95% CI (**EXPLORATORY**). The only **CONFIRMATORY** test behind the
figure is the three-way interaction `Poly:Inoc:Water` on grain allocation (panel C), reported in
`10_Rigor_Reversal/10_Reversal_Rigor.Rmd`.

The models are the same ones fit in `10_Reversal_Rigor.Rmd`: one full `Poly * Inoc * Water` model
per currency, on all 60 pots, contrasts conditioned inside it. This file re-fits them and then
**checks the plotted numbers against `10_Rigor_Reversal/outputs/reversal_simple_effects.csv`**, so
the figure cannot silently drift from the analysis.

| Panel | Response | Model | Plotted as |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | total NPP per plant | `gls`, `varIdent(~1\|Poly)` (selected in 10, Sec. 2b) | % change |
| B | grain mass per plant | `gls`, equal variance (selected in 10, Sec. 2b) | % change |
| C | grain allocation (**primary**) | beta, `dispformula = ~Poly` (pre-specified) | percentage points |

Sign convention: `Inoc - Strl`, asserted in code. Positive = inoculation increased the response.

```{r libs}
library(tidyverse)
library(emmeans)
library(glmmTMB)
library(nlme)

wheat <- readRDS("../wheat_audited.rds") %>%
  mutate(log_NPP = log(NPP), log_berry = log(berry))
stopifnot(nrow(wheat) == 60,
          identical(levels(wheat$Inoc), c("Inoc", "Strl")),
          identical(levels(wheat$Water), c("Control", "Moderate", "Severe")))
```

# Models and effect sizes

```{r models}
# weights object spliced into the call (bquote) so emmeans can re-evaluate it; see 10_Reversal_Rigor.Rmd
fit_gls <- function(y, w = NULL) {
  f <- reformulate("Poly*Inoc*Water", y)
  eval(bquote(gls(.(f), weights = .(w), data = wheat, method = "REML")))
}
m_npp   <- fit_gls("log_NPP",   varIdent(form = ~ 1 | Poly))
m_berry <- fit_gls("log_berry")
m_alloc <- glmmTMB(berry_alloc ~ Poly * Inoc * Water, dispformula = ~ Poly,
                   family = beta_family(), data = wheat)

tidy_contrast <- function(model, panel_label, scale = c("log", "response")) {
  scale <- match.arg(scale)
  emm <- emmeans(model, ~ Inoc | Poly * Water, data = wheat)
  if (scale == "response") emm <- regrid(emm)
  # "pairwise" = first level minus second = Inoc - Strl.
  # NOT "revpairwise": with levels (Inoc, Strl) that gives Strl - Inoc and mirrors the figure.
  ct <- contrast(emm, "pairwise", by = c("Poly", "Water"), adjust = "none")
  d  <- as.data.frame(summary(ct, infer = c(TRUE, TRUE)))
  stopifnot(all(d$contrast == "Inoc - Strl"))
  lo <- intersect(c("asymp.LCL", "lower.CL"), names(d))[1]
  hi <- intersect(c("asymp.UCL", "upper.CL"), names(d))[1]
  out <- tibble(Poly = d$Poly, Water = d$Water, est = d$estimate, lo = d[[lo]], hi = d[[hi]])
  out <- if (scale == "log") mutate(out, across(c(est, lo, hi), ~ (exp(.x) - 1) * 100))  # % change
         else                mutate(out, across(c(est, lo, hi), ~ .x * 100))             # percentage points
  mutate(out, panel = panel_label)
}

panel_levels <- c("A. Total productivity (NPP)\n% change", "B. Grain mass\n% change", "C. Allocation to grain\npercentage points")
eff <- bind_rows(
  tidy_contrast(m_npp,   panel_levels[1], "log"),
  tidy_contrast(m_berry, panel_levels[2], "log"),
  tidy_contrast(m_alloc, panel_levels[3], "response")
) %>% mutate(panel = factor(panel, panel_levels),
             Poly  = factor(Poly, c("Mono", "Inter")),
             Water = factor(Water, c("Control", "Moderate", "Severe")))

# --- consistency check against the analysis document -------------------------------
chk <- read.csv("../10_Rigor_Reversal/outputs/reversal_simple_effects.csv") %>%
  mutate(panel = case_when(str_starts(currency, "A") ~ panel_levels[1],
                           str_starts(currency, "B") ~ panel_levels[2],
                           str_starts(currency, "C") ~ panel_levels[3]),
         Poly = factor(Poly, c("Mono", "Inter")), Water = factor(Water, c("Control", "Moderate", "Severe"))) %>%
  select(panel, Poly, Water, est_10 = est, lo_10 = lo, hi_10 = hi)
cmp <- eff %>% mutate(panel = as.character(panel)) %>%
  inner_join(chk %>% mutate(panel = as.character(panel)), by = c("panel", "Poly", "Water"))
stopifnot(nrow(cmp) == 18,
          max(abs(cmp$est - cmp$est_10), abs(cmp$lo - cmp$lo_10), abs(cmp$hi - cmp$hi_10)) < 1e-6)
cat("Figure estimates match 10_Reversal_Rigor outputs for all 18 contrasts.\n")
```

# Figure 1

```{r figure, fig.width=9.5, fig.height=4.2, dpi=150}
pal <- c(Mono = "#CC5500", Inter = "#2166ac")   # re-run validate_palette.js if these change
shp <- c(Mono = 16, Inter = 17)                  # shape = second, color-independent encoding
poly_lab <- c(Mono = "Monoculture (12 wheat)", Inter = "Wheat/ fava intercrop (6 wheat + 1 fava)")

water_lab <- c(Control = "Control", Moderate = "Moderate", Severe = "Severe")
signed <- function(x) ifelse(x > 0, paste0("+", x), as.character(x))

# Fixed x-offsets (equal to position_dodge(0.4) with two groups) so Mono sits in exactly the same
# place whether or not Inter is drawn. A plain dodge would re-center a lone group.
offset <- c(Mono = -0.1, Inter = 0.1)

# `d` is what gets drawn; axis ranges are always taken from the FULL effect table `eff`, so the
# monoculture-only version and the full version share identical panels and y-axes.
plot_fig1 <- function(d) {
  pos <- function(x) mutate(x, x = as.numeric(Water) + offset[as.character(Poly)])
  shown <- levels(droplevels(d$Poly))   # legend lists only the stand types actually drawn
  ggplot(pos(d), aes(x = x, y = est, color = Poly, shape = Poly, group = Poly)) +
    geom_blank(data = pos(eff), aes(y = lo)) +
    geom_blank(data = pos(eff), aes(y = hi)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = 2, color = "grey45", linewidth = 0.4) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.7, alpha = 0.85) +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), width = 0.12, linewidth = 0.6) +
    geom_point(size = 3, stroke = 0.6) +
    facet_wrap(~ panel, scales = "free_y", ncol = 3) +
    scale_color_manual(values = pal, labels = poly_lab[shown], breaks = shown) +
    scale_shape_manual(values = shp, labels = poly_lab[shown], breaks = shown) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:3, labels = water_lab, limits = c(0.5, 3.5)) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = scales::breaks_pretty(n = 6), labels = function(x) signed(x)) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "Effect of AMF inoculation\n(inoculated minus sterile)") +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.title = element_blank(),
          strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11, hjust = 0, lineheight = 1.05),
          panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
          panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "grey90", linewidth = 0.3),
          axis.text.x = element_text(lineheight = 0.9),
          panel.spacing.x = unit(1.1, "lines"))
}

fig1_mono <- plot_fig1(eff %>% filter(Poly == "Mono"))   # step 1: monoculture only
fig1      <- plot_fig1(eff)                              # step 2: monoculture + intercrop

dir.create("figures", showWarnings = FALSE)
ggsave("figures/Fig1a_Reversal_MonoOnly.pdf", fig1_mono, width = 9.5, height = 4.2)
ggsave("figures/Fig1a_Reversal_MonoOnly.png", fig1_mono, width = 9.5, height = 4.2, dpi = 300, bg = "white")
ggsave("figures/Fig1_Reversal.pdf", fig1, width = 9.5, height = 4.2)
ggsave("figures/Fig1_Reversal.png", fig1, width = 9.5, height = 4.2, dpi = 300, bg = "white")
```

## Step 1: monoculture only

```{r fig-mono, fig.width=9.5, fig.height=4.2, dpi=150}
print(fig1_mono)
```

## Step 2: monoculture plus the wheat/ fava intercrop

```{r fig-full, fig.width=9.5, fig.height=4.2, dpi=150}
print(fig1)
```

Units: panels A and B are percent change in the response (back-transformed from the log scale);
panel C is percentage points of allocation (grain as a share of total NPP). All y-axes are free
so each panel uses its own range; the dashed line is no effect in every panel.

## Proposed caption

> **Figure 1. In monoculture, AMF inoculation turns from a grain benefit to a grain cost as
> drought intensifies; in mixed stands it has no detectable effect.** Model-estimated effect of inoculation
> (inoculated minus sterile) on (A) total productivity, (B) grain mass, and (C) grain allocation
> (grain as a share of total net primary production) at three water levels (80, 60, 40% of field
> capacity), in monoculture (orange circles) and in mixed stands with fava bean (blue triangles).
> Points are estimates from a single model per response fitted to all 60 pots; bars are 95%
> confidence intervals, unadjusted for multiplicity; the dashed line marks no effect. Every
> contrast is computed within a stand type and water level, so planting density is constant within
> each contrast and does not contribute to any estimate. n = 5 pots per cell. Panels A and B are
> percent change on the response scale (from log-scale models), panel C is percentage points.
> The confirmatory test is the three-way interaction on grain allocation (Poly x Inoc x Water,
> p = 0.00025); the contrasts plotted here are exploratory descriptions of that interaction.
> At the control water level, inoculation raised total productivity and grain mass in monoculture,
> but the allocation estimate there includes zero.

## Values plotted

```{r table}
eff %>% arrange(panel, Poly, Water) %>%
  transmute(panel, Poly, Water,
            estimate = round(est, 1), `95% CI` = sprintf("[%.1f, %.1f]", lo, hi),
            `CI excludes 0` = ifelse(lo > 0 | hi < 0, "yes", "no")) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Values plotted in Figure 1 (EXPLORATORY; unadjusted 95% CIs).")
```
